title: Broadcom to lend Anthropic up to $42B in deal to lease chips
content:
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) has inked a series of deals with tech heavyweights ranging from Amazon to Microsoft to both finance and provide computing capacity for the company's AI models.
All three have raised concerns about circular financing, as each firm provides funding to Anthropic, which then uses it to purchase their services.
Now you can add Broadcom (AVGO) to the list. According to Reuters, which obtained Anthropic's IPO prospectus, Broadcom is lending up to $42 billion to Anthropic for its infrastructure buildout.
In turn, Anthropic is estimated to spend so much on Broadcom's technologies that the Claude developer will become the chip designer's largest compute customer by 2027.
In April, Anthropic announced it was teaming up with Broadcom and Google for a deal that would see Google provide its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) capacity to Anthropic, with the supply coming online in 2027.
Broadcom designs Google's TPUs.
Anthropic isn't just purchasing chips, though. The company is also leaning on Broadcom for equipment leasing and financing, Reuters reports.
Wall Street analysts and investors have raised concerns about circular investing at multiple points throughout the AI buildout. Broadcom rivals Nvidia and AMD have also provided funding to their own customers, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which the labs then used to pay for access to the companies' high-powered chips.
The concern about such financial schemes is that if one domino in the row falls, it will cause a chain reaction that will decimate the AI trade and, as a result, the global equities markets that have benefited from and come to rely on such firms to keep the good times on Wall Street rolling.

report.summary: Broadcom will lend Anthropic up to $42B to lease chips, deepening circular AI financing as Anthropic is expected to become Broadcom's largest compute customer by 2027.
report.background: Anthropic has struck infrastructure and financing deals with Amazon, Microsoft, and now Broadcom, raising concerns about circular AI financing. In this model, a chipmaker or cloud provider funds an AI lab, which then spends the money on that provider's hardware or services. Broadcom already designs Google's TPUs; in April, Anthropic said it would team with Broadcom and Google for TPU capacity starting in 2027. Reuters reports Broadcom is lending Anthropic up to $42 billion for infrastructure, plus equipment leasing and financing. Analysts worry that such vendor financing inflates demand and creates systemic risk. If one AI lab or supplier falters, the chain of investments, chip orders, and cloud contracts could unwind, threatening the broader AI trade and global equities that have rallied around it.
key_points: Broadcom is lending Anthropic up to $42 billion for infrastructure buildout, according to Reuters, which obtained Anthropic's IPO prospectus. The support covers chip purchases and equipment leasing/financing, deepening ties between the chip designer and the Claude developer.

By 2027, Anthropic is estimated to become Broadcom's largest compute customer, spending heavily on Broadcom-designed technologies. In April, Anthropic announced a deal with Broadcom and Google for Google TPU capacity starting in 2027; Broadcom designs Google's TPUs.

The arrangement is the latest example of circular financing: a vendor funds a customer, which then buys the vendor's chips or services. Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia, and AMD have similar deals with AI labs, blurring the lines between investor, supplier, and customer.

Wall Street analysts and investors fear a domino effect. If one AI lab or supplier stumbles, funding, chip orders, and cloud contracts could cascade, potentially hitting AI stocks and the global equities markets that rely on the AI trade.

The disclosure in Anthropic's IPO prospectus signals the Claude maker is formalizing massive infrastructure commitments as it moves toward public markets, even as scrutiny of vendor financing and AI-bubble risks intensifies.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the deal reinforces vendor financing as a core growth engine, accelerating compute buildout while increasing systemic risk. For developers, Anthropic's expanded compute could mean more capable Claude models and API capacity, but if financing unwinds, access and pricing may shift. It also strengthens Broadcom and Google TPUs as alternatives to Nvidia. For regular users, better AI products may arrive faster, yet a correction could bring consolidation, higher prices, or service disruptions. Regulators may scrutinize circular deals, disclosure, and antitrust. Overall, compute is now strategic currency, and financial engineering is central to the AI race.
report.tools: To follow: Broadcom's custom AI ASICs and Google TPUs; Anthropic's Claude API; open-source inference stacks like vLLM and SGLang for running models on alternative hardware; MLPerf for chip benchmarks. For financial tracking, watch AVGO, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT filings and IPO prospectus. Open-source LLMs like Llama and Mistral offer alternatives if closed-model costs rise.
